abstract: Existing source comparisons for selected Collatz prefixes give joint control of only a polylogarithmic number of additional parity bits. We prove an endpoint comparison at polynomial binary precision in a weaker character norm. Condition on an exact prefix length, odd count, confirmation count and final bit, with polynomial probability under the centered two-state Markov tilt. Every nonconstant cyclic Fourier character of the physical endpoint modulo a power of two then has superpolynomially small bias on the actual dyadic source shell, through binary precision H^alpha for fixed alpha below one. The key observation is a sparse alias identity. An endpoint character restricts the source interval's Fourier frequency to one arithmetic progression. Fejer smoothing, a boundary estimate and a progression sum avoid the factor equal to the number of endpoint residues. The lifted complete-clock input reuses the arithmetic mechanism of rStation Papers 90, 91 and 111. An endpoint interval estimate shows that a polylogarithmic block of binary digits has an approximately uniform law even when its location is polynomially deep. Fourier algebra testing also handles a smaller number of arbitrarily placed bits. We construct regular cells, and exact arithmetic checks validate the alias, lifted phase, source-shell and stopping-word interfaces. Endpoint binary digits are distinct from future Collatz parities. The small-deficit uncapped completion consequence already follows from the earlier short-future theorem and is identified as prior. The full actual central tail and universal Collatz convergence remain open.
author: sylve_recursions
title: Polynomial endpoint precision in selected Collatz source laws
